method_note: All verified=false: page fetches were denied, figures come from search-result summaries only. retail_twh values are approximate (EIA-scale) and not sourced. 1 c/kWh over 1 TWh = $10M.

channels.source: Utility Dive / PUCT; Sierra Club ($33B STEP)
channels.basis: PUCT approved 765 kV Permian plan Apr 2025; STEP ~$33B, socialized across ERCOT. Full plan ~$4B/yr (12% carrying) / ~450 TWh = 0.88c; ~half data centers -> 0.44c high once built. Little in rates today. TPPF (opposed) claims >$200/household/yr all-in.
Energy-only market, no capacity market. IMM 2024 report not opened; no data-center-attributed price effect found.
channels.source: Potomac Economics 2024 State of the Market

channels.basis: 765 kV plan about $33B total (Permian piece about $13.8B), approved Apr 2025. Annual revenue requirement at roughly 12% of capex would be about $4B/yr at full build (my arithmetic), under 1 c/kWh on 480 TWh. Drivers mixed: oil and gas first, data centers second. Little is in rates yet. Cost allocation to large loads still under review.
channels.source: Sierra Club summary of ERCOT filing; Utility Dive; TPPF

recommended.one_line_basis: Transmission is the only channel: partial share of a build-out only starting to reach rates, split with oil and gas. Not computed from a measured figure.

ERCOT.notes: No official estimate. Energy-only market, so no capacity channel. Large-load cost allocation unresolved. LBNL finds high-load-growth states saw real prices fall 2019-2024, which may include Texas (unconfirmed).

checked.source: Utility Dive / PUCT; Sierra Club ($33B STEP)
checked.note: PUCT approved 765 kV Permian plan Apr 2025; STEP ~$33B, socialized across ERCOT. Full plan ~$4B/yr (12% carrying) / ~450 TWh = 0.88c; ~half data centers -> 0.44c high once built. Little in rates today. TPPF (opposed) claims >$200/household/yr all-in.

channels.basis: CAISO approved >$2B South Bay Area network upgrades (May 2025) for 2.5 GW of data-center and electrification load, 2026-2039; socialized across CAISO under FERC rules. ~$2B x ~12%/yr carrying charge = ~$240M/yr once in service, upper bound (shared with electrification).

recommended.one_line_basis: $240M/yr upper bound / ~215 TWh CAISO retail = 0.11c when fully in service; little in rates today; PG&E claims load growth lowers rates (company claim, 1-2% per GW).

CAISO.notes: Verified Cal Advocates page 2025-10-28. PG&E says residential rates ~11% lower Jan 2026 vs Jan 2024 and credits load growth in part (company claim). CPUC opened a large-load rate design rulemaking in Apr 2026.

channels.basis: 2025/26 PRA summer $666.50/MW-day; annual ~10x. Most MISO load is self-supplied by vertically integrated utilities, so auction prices reach few retail bills (e.g., Ameren Illinois). No IMM data-center attribution.

2025/26 PRA about $217/MW-day annualized. At about 125 GW (my assumption) that is roughly $9.9B/yr, about $9B above the prior year. The spike is mostly shrinking surplus and the new demand curve. Assumed 10-15% data-center attribution gives about $1B. 2026/27 fell about 42% to about $120/MW-day, so about $0.6B.
channels.source: Utility Dive / Modo Energy / Enel on MISO PRA

channels.basis: Entergy Louisiana/Meta: $3.2B for 3 gas plants approved Aug 2025, with Meta minimum bills; 7 more plants requested Apr 2026. Critics warn of stranded-asset risk. Residential effect disputed (about +/-$1/mo to +$8/mo).
channels.source: S&P Global; UCS; Axios New Orleans

recommended.one_line_basis: About $1B of data-center-attributed capacity cost (my assumed 10-15% of the 2025/26 spike) over 600 TWh is about 0.17 c; 2026/27 prices are lower.

MISO.notes: No MISO market monitor attribution found. Data-center share of the capacity spike is my assumption. Large-load forecast (34 to 218 TWh by 2035) is future, not current. Missouri, Kansas and Indiana have large-load tariffs.

checked.note: 2025/26 PRA summer $666.50/MW-day; annual ~10x. Most MISO load is self-supplied by vertically integrated utilities, so auction prices reach few retail bills (e.g., Ameren Illinois). No IMM data-center attribution.

channels.basis: Evergy large-load tariffs approved KS 2025-11-06 and MO 2025-11-14 to recover all large-load costs; MO SB4 bars shifting to residential.

No capacity market. Utility-level: Evergy LLPS tariff (over 75 MW) designed to cover incremental cost; Missouri 2025 law bars shifting large-load costs to residential. PSO got a 3.55% increase in Nov 2026 plus a new large-load tariff. No $ attribution found.
channels.source: Kansas KCC; Missouri PSC fact sheet; GCN on Oklahoma PSO

recommended.one_line_basis: No market-level channel and tariffs designed to protect residential customers. Central is a small placeholder, not a calculation.

SPP.notes: Evidence is thin. Large-load tariffs (Evergy, PSO, OG&E pending) aim to make data centers cover their incremental cost. Intervenors dispute some protections. Data-center buildout is mostly future.

checked.note: Evergy large-load tariffs approved KS 2025-11-06 and MO 2025-11-14 to recover all large-load costs; MO SB4 bars shifting to residential.

official_estimate.what: ISO-NE stated (Feb 2026 letter to senators) that data centers have not yet been a driver of wholesale costs, with little development in the region.
official_estimate.source: ISO-NE letter responding to senators; ISO Newswire

channels.basis: ISO-NE: large loads not yet a major driver of load growth; a couple hundred MW in formal study.
2026 CELT large-load forecast only about 110 MW in the 2030s, negligible against a roughly 25 GW peak. Proposed rules would keep large loads out of capacity demand curves.

recommended.one_line_basis: ISO-NE says data centers are not yet a driver of wholesale cost; forecast large load is about 110 MW.

ISO-NE.notes: Rated official only because ISO-NE self-reports, and I did not open the letter. New England rates are high for other reasons (gas, transmission, policy). Senators asked in Jan 2026 how residents will be shielded.

checked.note: ISO-NE: large loads not yet a major driver of load growth; a couple hundred MW in formal study.

channels.basis: Few large data centers connected yet; forecast growth through 2030 largely large loads (Modo summary of NYISO forecast, not confirmed).
No NYISO or MMU data-center attribution found. Queue holds about 6 GW across 29 large-load proposals, but the forecast counts only likely projects, so current effect is small.
channels.source: Modo Energy on NYISO demand forecast; NYISO Power Trends 2026

recommended.one_line_basis: No evidence of a measurable current data-center cost; placeholder near zero given the small operating load.

NYISO.notes: Very thin evidence. Existing crypto and data load is modest. Forecast growth is dominated by electrification and large industrial and chip fabs, with data centers a minority.

checked.note: Few large data centers connected yet; forecast growth through 2030 largely large loads (Modo summary of NYISO forecast, not confirmed).

channels.basis: PSC staff warned of $20+/mo; Dec 2025 settlement: Georgia Power guarantees large-load revenue 2029-2031 so the $20 increase does not materialize, plus $8.50/mo downward pressure pledge in 2028. Staff: DC forecasts overestimated. Others (Duke etc.) no figure.

Georgia Power: PSC staff say its 10 GW build-out could raise residential bills at least $20/mo by 2030 (future). Company claims $2.89/mo downward pressure in 2026-28. Base rates frozen through 2028. About 80% of the 69 GW pipeline is data centers.
channels.source: AJC; Georgia PSC; Georgia Power press release

channels.basis: Duke Carolinas: data centers are over 85% of expected economic-development load growth (8 GW added through 2035). NC approved a 2-year increase from Jan 2027 with new data-center rules. Duke declined to say what share is data-center driven.

recommended.one_line_basis: Georgia's $20/mo by 2030 is about 1.8 c/kWh for GA, about 0.3 c region-wide at full impact; today's effect is a fraction of that.

Southeast non-RTO.notes: Vertically integrated, so costs flow into rate cases, mostly 2026-2030. Large-load rules (GA Jan 2025, NC Nov 2026) and minimum bills aim to protect residential customers. Many GA contracts predate the rules per PSC staff.

checked.note: PSC staff warned of $20+/mo; Dec 2025 settlement: Georgia Power guarantees large-load revenue 2029-2031 so the $20 increase does not materialize, plus $8.50/mo downward pressure pledge in 2028. Staff: DC forecasts overestimated. Others (Duke etc.) no figure.

channels.basis: APS asks ~45% increase for the data-center class (XHLF) vs ~14% residential to avoid subsidies; case pending at ACC.

APS: data centers about 5-7% of peak. Rate case proposes residential +14-16% but data centers +45%, framed to avoid cross-subsidy. Ruling expected end of 2026. No NV Energy or other utility figures found.

recommended.one_line_basis: Data centers are about 5-7% of APS peak and are assigned larger increases than residential; placeholder, not computed.

West non-RTO.notes: Evidence thin and AZ-only. LBNL notes New Mexico saw real price declines with large data center and industrial additions. Much of the Western residential increase is wildfire, transmission and gas cost, not data centers.

checked.note: APS asks ~45% increase for the data-center class (XHLF) vs ~14% residential to avoid subsidies; case pending at ACC.
